exposure: Umbilical cord blood gases (venous and arterial pH, base excess, PCO2, lactate)
cohort: 150 singleton live-born infants between 34 and 42 weeks of gestation with no major anomalies, enrolled from November 2015 to March 2016, in delivery unit of obstetrics and gynecology ward, Imam Hossein Medical Center, Tehran, Iran
finding: Significant differences were found in umbilical cord blood gases and Apgar scores between infants with and without intrapartum distress.
